upheld.problem: The live-tick pipeline is unconditionally synchronous regardless of N. Its cost is Θ(V), not Θ(K): the repair's partition sweep touches every view entry, the merge writes a full new permutation (4 MB of int at 1M rows, ~8–16 MB of memory traffic per tick with scratch), and §2.5 then re-derives groups AND rebuilds the flattened view O(V) — two more full passes with a compiled SameGroup call per adjacent pair plus two ~4–8 MB array writes. At 1M grouped rows that is realistically 5–15 ms per coalesced tick ON THE UI THREAD, every frame the feed ticks — the exact headline scenario ("live-updating feed demo, large dataset"). Invariant 5 ("UI thread never hitches on a big reshape") is violated by the tick path it doesn't cover. The 100k sub-ms claim may hold; nothing in the design holds at 1M.
upheld.amendment: In §2.6, size-gate the live-tick pipeline the same way full reshapes are gated: when V (visible view size, or N ungrouped) exceeds a TickBackgroundThreshold, run the coalesced tick's repair + regroup + flatten on the ThreadPool as a mini-reshape over the existing sealed-snapshot machinery (dirty keys re-extracted before departure; ticks arriving mid-shape queue and fold into the next tick-shape; at most one in flight per the existing one-shape-at-a-time/version-stamp rules; result publishes via IShapingScheduler.Post with the atomic snapshot swap). Keep the synchronous path below the threshold — it remains the common case at ≤100k. Reconcile invariant 4 by either adding the small-K in-place displacement repair (binary-search reposition, O(K log N + K·moves)) that its 'typical' complexity claims, or rewording the invariant to the sweep+merge's actual O(N + K log K). Record this as the answer to open question 3 (O(V) regroup per tick is acceptable only under the gate). Add a '1M rows, grouped, live-tick (K∈{1,100,1k})' row to the §6 benchmark table as the gate's acceptance evidence, measuring both the background tick latency and the UI-thread cost per frame (publish + swap only).

upheld.problem: Load-bearing false assumption, verified against Cursorial.UI/Controls/SelectionModel.cs. (a) It is keyed on VIEW indices and its only fixups are ItemsInserted/ItemsRemoved/ItemsMoved/Reset — there is no permutation hook. Every K-repair tick and every re-sort PERMUTES the view arbitrarily, so after any live tick the selected view-indices point at different rows: selection silently migrates to other rows. Mapping a repair onto block-Move calls is not possible in general. (b) Scale: Ctrl+A at 1M rows = a 1M-entry HashSet<int> (~50 MB) and every structural op does an O(selected) allocating rebuild (Reindex/ItemsRemoved allocate a fresh HashSet + lists per op) — per live insert on a large selection that's an O(1M) alloc storm.
upheld.amendment: In §5, replace the 'SelectionModel … as-is' bullet: DataGrid row selection is keyed on stable row ids (RowStore slots), not view indices — ids survive every repair/re-sort/regroup untouched, so reshape requires zero selection fixup; id↔view-index translation happens only at gesture and paint time via the snapshot's permutation plus a maintained inverse-permutation (id → view index) lookup. Represent large selections compactly: sorted id ranges and/or an 'all-except' inversion for select-all, so Shift+Ctrl+End / Ctrl+A at 1M rows is O(1)-ish, not a 1M-entry HashSet. Anchor/lead and Shift-range semantics are computed in view space by the grid's gesture mapper, then stored as ids. SelectionModel stays as-is for ListBox/TabControl; the DataGrid gets its own id-space selection controller (factored reusable for ListView/TreeListView per invariant 7), or SelectionModel gains an explicit id-space mode with bulk-set — either way the 'as-is' reuse claim is dropped. Removal of a row drops its id from the selection (with lead relocation computed in view space); §6's test matrix gains rows pinning selection identity across randomized repair/re-sort tick streams.

upheld.problem: Two defects. (1) The claimed 'typical' O(K log N + K·moves) is not achievable by the described algorithm: the partition sweep reads all N view entries and the merge writes all N — it is Θ(N) per cycle, always. The doc's typical-case claim is false as written and will mislead the threshold analysis (Q2). (2) The merge as described performs ~N invocations of the compiled multi-column Comparison<int> (one per emitted element until a side exhausts). Each compare does 2+ random indexed loads keys[view[i]] into multi-MB key vectors — cache-miss-bound, ~5–15 ns each → the compare cost alone is multiple ms at 1M and is what makes even the 100k "sub-millisecond" claim borderline. The full-sort section specifies galloping; the repair merge doesn't.
upheld.amendment: In §2.3, replace the complexity claims with the honest model: Θ(N) index traffic per repair cycle + O(K log K) dirty sort + O(K·log(N/K)) comparer calls; amend invariant 4 (line 23) to match (drop the unsupported "O(K log N + K·moves) typical"). Specify the repair merge as a GALLOPING merge: exponential/binary-search each sorted dirty element's insertion point within the clean run, bulk-copy (Array.Copy/memmove) the intervening clean gaps, so comparer invocations fall from ~N to O(K log(N/K)) and the pass is memory-bandwidth-bound. Re-derive the K > ~N/8 fallback threshold (Q2) from this cost model — the crossover vs adaptive full TimSort is between Θ(N)-bandwidth+O(K log(N/K))-compares repair and the mostly-sorted TimSort path, and should be confirmed by the §6 benchmark table rather than asserted.

upheld.problem: Boxing is a rounding error next to the unaddressed dominant cost: culture-aware (or case-insensitive) string comparison goes through ICU at ~100–300 ns per call. A 1M-row full sort ≈ 20M compares ≈ 2–6 SECONDS; even the repair merge's O(K log N) compares hitch visibly. No competitive grid sorts large string columns by calling string.Compare per comparison.
upheld.amendment: Amend §2.2 (and touch §2.3/§2.6 accordingly): for string columns with a non-Ordinal StringComparison, key extraction produces COLLATION KEYS, not string references — CompareInfo.GetSortKeyLength(ReadOnlySpan<char>) + GetSortKey(ReadOnlySpan<char>, Span<byte>) into one pooled per-column byte blob with an (offset,length) pair per slot; the compiled comparer for such columns becomes ReadOnlySpan<byte>.SequenceCompareTo (SIMD ordinal memcmp). Ordinal string columns skip key materialization and use string.CompareOrdinal directly (already memcmp-speed). The key-vector abstraction in §2.2 must therefore admit two representations (typed TKey[] vs byte-range vectors), visible to the multi-column Comparison<int> codegen, the Min/Max aggregator path, dirty-row re-extraction in §2.3's repair, and §2.6's sealed-snapshot rule (the blob seals with the key vectors). Original strings remain the source for formatting, distinct-value lists, and contains/starts-with filters — collation keys are sort/group-order-only. Note the memory tradeoff (roughly string-length-order bytes per row, pooled, only for non-Ordinal-configured columns). Restate invariant 2 so the hot-path rule covers per-compare cost, not just boxing. The StringComparison default (Ordinal vs culture) is left as a separate explicit decision — with collation keys either default is affordable.

upheld.problem: Three holes. (1) SLOT REUSE: a queued INCC Remove eventually frees the slot to the free list; if a queued Add reuses that slot before the in-flight shape publishes (or while the PUBLISHED snapshot's permutation still references it), the row id aliases a different row — the merge is corrupted and the band cache formats the wrong row. Nothing in the design defers reclamation. (2) EXTRACTION SITING: "key vectors it extracted before departure" puts O(N) extraction (1M getter calls + string/sort-key materialization for a NEW sort column) on the UI thread before departure — precisely the hitch invariant 5 exists to prevent. (3) REPLAY ORDERING: INCC and INPC pending ticks must replay as ONE FIFO in arrival order (an INPC on a row a queued Remove precedes must resolve against the pre-remove id map), and a superseded/cancelled shape's pending queue must transfer whole to its successor — neither is stated.
upheld.amendment: Amend §2.6 (and record as the §7 Q5 answer, pinned in the DV ledger): (a) slot reclamation is deferred — a freed slot returns to the free list only when no in-flight shape and no published snapshot references it (generation stamp or refcount on free-list entries, swept at publish/supersede; RowStore.RemoveAt must not Push immediately); (b) key extraction for columns newly entering the shape runs IN the background phase against the sealed row-reference snapshot, with the torn-read-of-mutating-user-rows caveat documented as accepted (DevExpress posture) — never O(N) extraction on the UI thread before departure; (c) INCC and INPC pending ticks form ONE FIFO queue in arrival order, each tick resolving against the id map of its arrival epoch, and a superseded shape's pending queue transfers whole to its successor on cancellation.

upheld.problem: Deterministic, yes (and a−b can't overflow for non-negative ids) — but the tie ORDER is slot-allocation order, which free-list reuse makes arbitrary relative to source order and unstable across a session: remove any row, add a new one, and the newcomer reuses a low slot — it sorts ABOVE all its equal-key peers instead of below (WPF/DevExpress semantics: ties keep source order). Users see equal-key rows reshuffle depending on deletion history. This also degrades the repair path's UX: re-inserted rows jump rather than append within their tie class.
upheld.amendment: In §2.1, add a slot-aligned monotonically increasing insertion-sequence vector (e.g. `ulong[] _seq`, stamped from a per-store counter every time a slot is occupied or re-occupied; grown with the other key vectors). In §2.2, change the multi-column comparer's final tiebreak from row-id `a − b` to comparing `_seq[a]` vs `_seq[b]` (a proper compare, not subtraction, if the sequence type can exceed int range). Row id remains the identity/index space everywhere else. Amend the §1/§2.2 wording to state the delivered semantics precisely: ties order by insertion sequence, stable across arbitrary add/remove history, preserving the total order, unique binary-search positions, and determinism.

upheld.problem: The snapshot is not sealed — it is the live RowStore arrays, and the design as written leaves three mutation paths open while the ThreadPool shape reads them. (1) Slot reuse: §2.1's free-list reuses a removed row's slot for a mid-shape INCC Add; if the Add's key extraction is eager (the doc never says when Adds extract), the shaper's in-flight permutation still references that slot as the OLD row while its key vector now holds the NEW row's keys — a torn, order-inconsistent comparer. (2) Key-vector growth on Add reallocates TKey[]; harmless only if the shaper is guaranteed to hold the pre-departure array reference, which the doc doesn't pin. (3) Any synchronous small-repair running during an in-flight background shape (the doc only says pending ticks 'replay on completion', but §2.6 also says small work 'runs synchronously' — the two rules conflict when a tick arrives mid-shape) re-extracts dirty keys in place. An inconsistent Comparison<int> is not just wrong output: TimSort's galloping merge invariants break on comparator inconsistency (the well-known 'IComparer violates contract' failure mode in Array.Sort; a hand-rolled TimSort can index out of range or corrupt the permutation).
upheld.amendment: Amend §2.6 with pinned hard invariants for the background-shape window (departure → publish): (a) key vectors and the Sequences array are written ONLY on the owner thread and NEVER while a shape is in flight — a mid-shape INCC Add/Replace defers its RowStore slot op and key extraction into the pending-tick queue (extraction happens at replay, consistent with §2.3 repair step 2); (b) the free list is frozen while a shape is in flight — slots freed by mid-shape Removes become reusable only after publish, so an in-flight permutation's slot ids can never be re-bound; (c) reconcile with the codegen's read-through-the-field rule: the comparer MAY read Keys/Sequences through the live fields BECAUSE (a)+(b) guarantee no write or reallocation occurs mid-flight, and departure establishes the happens-before edge (all owner-thread extraction/sequence writes complete before the ThreadPool work item is queued — the queue is the fence; state this explicitly); (d) make explicit that while a shape is in flight the synchronous small-repair lane is suspended — ALL ticks (including their RowStore mutations, not just their repair work) queue and replay in order on the owner thread after publish. Add a dataviews-matrix row exercising the scenario: background reshape in flight + Remove then Add (slot-reuse pressure) + INPC ticks, asserting the published permutation equals the LINQ oracle and no torn state is observable; and a stress/property test that races ticks against background shapes to catch regressions of (a)–(d).

upheld.problem: The band window is NOT part of the public seam. IScrollContentHost carries extent/viewport/steps only; ScrollContentPresenter.BandStartRow, BandLength, and BandAnchorRow are internal (ScrollContentPresenter.cs:203–212), and the sanctioned precedent reads them cross-member as internals from the same assembly (VirtualizingStackPanel.cs:163–164 via _scrollOwner.BandStartRow). A direct-draw content MUST know the exact band: the zone scene is exactly [BandStartRow, BandStartRow+BandLength) with the ambient −BandStartRow translate (RenderTree.OnDrawZone:476–477), so under-painting the band leaves blank scene rows that an in-band composite slide reveals with zero further Render calls, and guessing from ScrollOffsetRow is wrong because bandStart = anchor−K is anchored at the last re-anchor, not the current offset. The doc's plan works only through InternalsVisibleTo (already added to Cursorial.UI.csproj), which contradicts both the 'public seam' framing and invariant 7's 'second sanctioned virtualization idiom' claim — no consumer outside the solution can implement a direct-draw scroll content correctly.
upheld.amendment: Promote the band window into the public scrolling contract and re-base both consumers on it. Either (a) add a push method to IScrollContentHost — e.g. void SetRealizationWindow(int startRow, int length) — invoked by ScrollContentPresenter at every site that calls InvalidateRealization and at arrange-end band-geometry refresh, or (b) make BandStartRow/BandLength public get-only members on ScrollContentPresenter, documented as "render-band geometry: the zone scene covers content rows [BandStartRow, BandStartRow+BandLength) and is drawn under an ambient −BandStartRow translate; a direct-draw IScrollContentHost content must paint exactly this window." VirtualizingStackPanel switches from its internal cross-member reads (VirtualizingStackPanel.cs ~163–164) to the same public surface, so one idiom serves both lanes. Amend dataviews-design.md §3.1/§3.2 to reference the public band contract instead of the internal members, and state in §5 that this promotion (not InternalsVisibleTo) is what makes direct-draw a genuinely sanctioned second virtualization idiom implementable outside the solution; keep the DataViews IVT entries only if still needed for unrelated internals.

upheld.problem: The presenter's Bounds is the full arranged extent (SCP ArrangeOverride arranges content at max(Extent, Viewport) — 1M rows at 1M view rows). If the presenter ever satisfies a boundary predicate — Opacity < 1, non-zero RenderOffset, ClipToBounds, or CompositeClip (UIElement.Render.cs:36–44), any of which a style, transition, or storyboard can set — it mints its own zone, and RenderTree.EnsureScene rents a scene sized to zone.Boundary.Bounds.Size (RenderTree.cs:428) because the SCP-banding special case applies only when the BOUNDARY IS the ScrollContentPresenter (line 438). That is a 1,000,000-row × ~300-column scene rent — multi-GB, instant death. The trap is easy to walk into: DrawnContentPresenter, the framework's existing direct-draw base, sets ClipToBounds = true in its constructor, so deriving the rows presenter from it (the obvious choice) triggers exactly this. The same latent hazard exists today for VirtualizingStackPanel content, unguarded.
upheld.amendment: In §3.2, pin: DataGridRowsPresenter derives UIElement directly (explicitly NOT DrawnContentPresenter — its constructor sets ClipToBounds = true, which makes the presenter a render boundary from attach); the presenter must never set ClipToBounds/CompositeClip/RenderOffset, and its theme/control styles must never set Opacity/RenderOffset/ClipToBounds on it (state looks are brush/attribute properties only, as already designed). Add an engine-side guard (solution-wide change): RenderTree.EnsureScene fails loudly with an actionable diagnostic naming the boundary element when a non-ScrollContentPresenter boundary's scene size exceeds a sanity ceiling (note the existing ScenePool.Rent ushort.MaxValue throw fires only above 65,535 rows and names nothing; sub-65,535 full-extent scenes currently rent hundreds of MB silently), plus a DEBUG assert in ScrollContentPresenter that its content element never becomes an effective render boundary. This also closes the identical latent hazard for VirtualizingStackPanel content.

upheld.problem: SelectionModel's indices are contiguous positional indices whose only maintenance ops are INCC-shaped shifts (ItemsInserted/ItemsRemoved/ItemsMoved/Reset — SelectionModel.cs:149–221). The grid's view index space is destroyed wholesale by every reshape: a K-row sort repair arbitrarily permutes view positions, a filter change drops/restores positions, and a group expand/collapse shifts EVERY subsequent flattened-view index. There is no permutation/remap operation, so selection stored in view-index space silently migrates onto the wrong rows after the very first live tick that moves rows — the exact steady operating mode of this control. Group rows also occupy view indices, so even range gestures need entry-kind filtering. 'As-is' does not hold, and the mapping is not ~30 lines.
upheld.amendment: Rewrite §5's selection bullet and add a §3.3 policy row: (1) Selection identity lives in ROW-ID (slot) space — membership survives re-sort/filter/regroup by construction; anchor and lead are stored as row ids. (2) Gestures materialize through the current DataViewSnapshot at event time: Shift-range walks the flattened view between anchor and lead positions collecting data-row entries only (group/summary entries excluded); hit row id resolves via the snapshot. (3) On source row removal the id is evicted from the selection set immediately (free-list slot reuse would otherwise resurrect selection onto an unrelated row). (4) Pin the filtered-out/collapsed policy: selected rows that become invisible (filter or collapse) REMAIN selected but hidden, DevExpress-style; SelectedItems reports them, the painter simply doesn't see them. (5) Realize this either by extending SelectionModel with a row-id mode plus targeted Deselect/remap ops (making it the invariant-7 reusable piece for ListView/TreeListView), or by a shaping-controller-owned RowSelection (row-id HashSet + anchor id + snapshot-time range materialization) — and drop the "as-is / ~30 lines" claim either way.

upheld.problem: 'Cheap relative to sort' is true for a full reshape but false for the live-tick path, where there is no full sort to hide behind: a K=1 tick under grouping at 1M visible rows still pays the O(V) SameGroup walk plus a full 1M-entry flattened-view rebuild — several ms of pure memory traffic per coalesced tick, every frame under a ticking feed. That violates invariant 5 on the control's headline scenario (large dataset + live shaping + grouping), and the sync/background split as designed cannot catch it because BackgroundThreshold gates on reshape kind/row count at reshape time, not on the per-tick regroup cost.
upheld.amendment: In §2.5/§2.6 (answering §7 Q3): make the sync/background decision cost-based per update cycle, not kind-based — a coalesced tick whose implied cost scales with V (the O(N) repair merge sweep + O(V) regroup + O(V) flatten) routes through the existing sealed-snapshot background lane when V exceeds a threshold (reusing the pending-tick replay machinery; benchmark-tune the crossover alongside the K/N repair threshold). The gate must cover the WHOLE tick cycle, since the repair sweep alone is O(N) even ungrouped. Additionally or alternatively, specify span-scoped incremental group repair: a K-row repair knows which view ranges moved, so re-derive only groups whose spans intersect moved rows and patch the flattened view by ranges (memmove); ticks on non-group columns that keep rows within their groups skip structural regroup entirely. Record in the doc that grouped 1M rows + live ticks is the scenario the chosen mechanism must keep hitch-free, with a benchmark row proving it.

upheld.problem: The doc contains NO column width model at all — no Width/MinWidth on columns, no star/fill sizing, no default-width rule for auto-generated columns, no header-edge resize gesture, no best-fit. Every horizontal fact in the design presupposes it: the logical-scroll extent, the cell x-range hit-test lookup ('column = x-range lookup'), header/filter/footer alignment, band-cache cell composition, and data-bar track width. The mockup pins explicit per-column ch widths (c-ord 11ch … c-stat 14ch). In DevExpress WPF, column Width/MinWidth + interactive resize + Best-Fit are table stakes, and best-fit is not paint-local: it needs formatted-string widths over (a sample of) rows, which reaches into the shaping engine's formatter kit and band cache — deciding it later reshapes the compiled-formatter contract (a 'measure formatted width' companion delegate, grapheme-aware via GraphemeWidth).
upheld.amendment: Add a §3.x "Column model and geometry" section: (1) a `DataGridColumn` presentation type (header caption, bound path or ShapedColumn link, alignment) with `Width` as a terminal GridLength analog — fixed cell count, `*` weights, and `Auto`; plus `MinWidth` (default ~4 cells). (2) Auto-generated columns default to Auto = max(header caption width + sort-glyph reserve + padding, MinWidth) clamped to a documented max (~30 cells), with Auto resolved from the header + the CURRENT band's formatted cells only (never a full-view scan). (3) Resolved widths recompute on column/width change and viewport resize; star columns distribute leftover viewport width after fixed/Auto, and when any star column is present extent.Width = viewport width (no horizontal scroll); otherwise extent.Width = Σ resolved widths — restate §3.1's GetExtent in these terms. (4) Interactive resize: a drag zone on each header cell's trailing boundary using the existing Thumb/GridSplitter screen-anchored-delta idiom, clamping to MinWidth, updating Width to a fixed value (breaking star/Auto, WPF parity). (5) Best-fit as v1 API (`BestFitColumn(s)`, double-click on the boundary may defer): computed UI-side via the column's compiled formatter + GraphemeWidth.StringWidth over the header + a bounded row sample — the current band by default, with an explicit opt-in full-view scan routed through the §2.6 background path above BackgroundThreshold; state that width measurement lives in the UI assembly, not the BCL-only shaping engine (invariant 1 unchanged). (6) Note the per-column x-range table as the single shared geometry artifact consumed by hit-testing, the band-cache painter, header/filter/footer alignment, data-bar track width, and the edit-row host.

upheld.problem: False in both candidate index spaces, and the doc never says which one it uses. (a) View-index space: a re-sort/refilter/regroup arbitrarily permutes view indices; SelectionModel has only ItemsInserted/ItemsRemoved/ItemsMoved shift hooks and Reset (verified in Cursorial.UI/Controls/SelectionModel.cs) — no permutation remap — so after any reshape the selected view indices point at different rows (selection visibly jumps to wrong rows), or Reset wipes it. DevExpress preserves selection identity across sort/filter/group. (b) Row-id (slot) space: ids are stable so identity survives, but SelectRangeFromAnchor and the shift hooks are meaningless in id space (Shift+click ranges are contiguous in VIEW order), and structural INCC ops don't shift slot ids at all. Additionally unspecified: what happens to selected rows that get filtered out, and whether the focus row follows its row object (identity) or its view position after a live-tick re-sort — in a ticking feed the focused row can move every frame, which is also a scroll-anchoring UX decision (DevExpress keeps focused row identity; it does not chase it with the viewport).
upheld.amendment: Rewrite §5's selection bullet and add a §3.3 subsection specifying identity-keyed selection with per-snapshot projection: (1) selection state is persisted as stable row ids (slots), never view indices; (2) gestures resolve in view space at gesture time — Shift ranges expand anchor..lead against the CURRENT snapshot's view order into an id set; (3) on each DataViewSnapshot publish, the grid re-projects selected ids to view indices for painting (O(selected) lookup via the snapshot's id→viewIndex map, or a bitset over slots consulted at paint); (4) row removal (slot freed) drops the id from selection at the RowStore event — before free-list reuse can recycle it. Implementation: either a new DataViews-owned SelectionController keyed on ids (with SelectionModel left to ListBox/TabControl), or extend SelectionModel with a public bulk ReplaceSelection(ISet<int>) + Remap(Func<int,int>) so a grid-side projection layer can drive it (reusable for ListView-over-shaping); the doc must pick one and drop the "as-is / ~30 lines" claim. Pin three policies: selected ids that get filtered out are retained-but-inert (restored when the filter releases them — DevExpress behavior); the focus row follows row IDENTITY across re-sorts/reshapes; the viewport does NOT auto-scroll to chase the focus row on live re-sorts (BringIntoView only on explicit navigation gestures).

upheld.problem: Shift+Enter and Shift+Space have NO legacy wire encoding — outside Kitty/modifyOtherKeys/Win32-input-mode they arrive as plain Enter/Space (this is exactly the capability gap the framework's own access-key gate exists for). So on legacy terminals 'append multi-sort' silently becomes 'replace sort' (destructive) and 'extend selection' becomes 'replace selection' — the keyboard path degrades worst precisely where keyboard is most needed. Separately: (a) Shift+Up/Down range extension — the universal grid gesture, and legacy-encodable (CSI 1;2A) — is missing entirely; (b) the sort cycle is unspecified (asc→desc→clear? how do you REMOVE a sort level or clear multi-sort from the keyboard?); (c) 'one-tab-stop' contradicts 'header … Tab stop'; (d) the auto-filter row is keyboard-unreachable in the stated model (Ctrl+Up from row 0 goes to the header — the filter row between them has no entry); (e) whether Left/Right focus-cell moves horizontally scroll the viewport (EnsureVisible on the column) is unstated.
upheld.amendment: Re-cut §3.3 terminal-safe: (1) Header band — Enter cycles the focused column's sort asc→desc→none (replace mode); Space appends/cycles the column as an additional sort level (both legacy-safe single keys); keep Shift+Enter/Shift+click as negotiated-capability aliases only, never the sole path. (2) Rows — Shift+Up/Down/PgUp/PgDn/Home/End are the primary range-extension gestures (legacy-encodable CSI modifier variants); Ctrl+Space toggles the focused row (NUL wire); drop Shift+Space from the spec. (3) Band model — the grid is exactly one Tab stop (strike the header 'Tab stop' phrase from line 245); internal bands cycle group panel ↔ header ↔ auto-filter row ↔ rows via Ctrl+Up/Ctrl+Down at the edges, giving the filter row its explicit stop between header and rows. (4) State the sort-cycle and multi-sort-removal semantics (Enter's none step removes the column's level; specify how a mid-list level removal renumbers). (5) State that Left/Right focus-cell moves call EnsureVisible on the target column's x-range (horizontal viewport follow), mirroring the vertical focus-row follow.

upheld.problem: The only grouping keyboard gesture in the doc is Ctrl+G on a focused header cell (add a level). There is no stated way to reach the chips at all, so everything the mockup's chips carry is mouse-only: remove (✕), reorder levels (the caption says 'reordering chips re-nests'), and toggling a group level's sort direction (chips carry ▲). 'Keyboard grouping' as claimed is therefore add-only — for a terminal control whose drag story is deferred, keyboard is the ONLY complete surface, and it can't ungroup or reorder.
upheld.amendment: In §3.3, add the group panel to the internal band cycle: from the header band, Ctrl+Up (or a stated equivalent) focuses the group panel when non-empty; Left/Right walk chips; Enter toggles the focused chip's group-level sort direction; Delete (and ✕ per the mockup) removes the level; Ctrl+Left/Right reorders levels (re-nests). Make Ctrl+G on a header cell a toggle: grouping an already-grouped column removes that group level. Update the §1 bullet to "keyboard (add/remove/reorder/sort-toggle) + API grouping; drag deferred" so the claim matches the surface.

upheld.problem: The mockup's rule taxonomy is six types (Highlight Cell, Top/Bottom, Data Bar, Color Scale, Icon Set, Expression), and its rules-manager grid explicitly lists a 'Color scale (heat)' rule; the doc's own §4 theme section ships heat-tint ThemeKeys — for a rule type the engine doesn't have. Highlight Cell and Icon Set fold into Threshold acceptably, but Color Scale (value→interpolated bg) and Top/Bottom (rank-based) do not: Top/Bottom needs column order statistics (k-th value / percentile) computed at reshape time — an engine hook on the same column-stats block DataBar's min/max already requires — not a paint-time concern. Leaving them out silently means the 'rules API is v1, dialogs later' deferral is false: the dialog can't target rule types that don't exist, so cutting the deferred seam later forces engine changes.
upheld.amendment: In §2.7, generalize DataBar's min/max anchors into a per-column stats block — min/max/requested percentiles/top-k cutoffs, computed via the existing compiled-aggregator machinery (§2.2 already has Min/Max) at reshape and patched at the same points as summaries on live ticks — and add two FormatRule variants reading it: ColorScale (2/3-stop anchors from stats, value→interpolated bg at paint, cached anchors so paint stays allocation-free) and TopBottom (Top/Bottom × Items/Percent → cached k-th-value cutoff, key comparison at paint). Also amend DataBar's anchor spec to allow number/percentile anchors (the mockup's own Data Bar dialog requires this). This makes §4's heat ThemeKeys and §1's 'rules API is v1, dialogs later' deferral internally consistent. If the owner instead rejects the scope, the fallback amendment is: move ColorScale and TopBottom to the §1 Deferred list explicitly (acknowledging the future dialog requires engine additions) and drop the heat-tint ThemeKeys from §4 v1.

upheld.problem: Two DevExpress group features the mockup implies don't fit the sort-prefix architecture, and neither is in v1 OR the deferred list: (a) sort-groups-by-summary (order Regions by Σ Amount — DevExpress GroupSummarySortInfo): group order then depends on aggregates computed AFTER grouping, which a prepended sort column cannot express; if the flatten never anticipates a group-level reorder pass, adding it later reworks §2.5. (b) The mockup dedicates a full section to group summaries 'Aligned under column' (a per-group footer row rendered in column positions, plus a Header/Footer placement toggle) and to the footer/group summary right-click quick menus + editor dialogs — all silently absent. The aligned variant adds a third structural row kind to a packed encoding specified with only two.
upheld.amendment: In §2.5: (1) specify the packed flatten entry with 2 row-kind bits from day one — data / group header / group footer / reserved (at 1M rows a 30-bit payload is ample in an int32 entry); (2) specify the flatten as group-TREE-driven (walk GroupNodes in display order emitting each node's contiguous {FirstViewIndex, RowCount} view range) rather than boundary-driven over the sorted view, and note that sibling-group display order is therefore an optional comparator pass over sibling GroupNode ranges before flatten — architecturally free since the flatten already rebuilds O(V) per reshape. In §1 Deferred, add explicitly: (a) sort-groups-by-summary (DevExpress GroupSummarySortInfo — rides the sibling-comparator pass above); (b) aligned-under-column group summaries + the group-summary Header/Footer placement (rides the group-footer row kind; one cell row, so §3.1's EstimateItemAt(r)=r math is unchanged); (c) the column/group summary right-click quick menus and summary editor dialogs (defer with the conditional-formatting manager/rule dialogs already listed).

upheld.problem: The doc never defines the *grid-facing* column API, and the engine's generic column cannot be it. The grid is necessarily non-generic (`ItemsSource : IEnumerable`, per the `ItemsControl` precedent at Cursorial.UI/Controls/ItemsControl.cs:21-55), and the XAML loader rejects generic instantiation outright — `x:TypeArguments` is CUR1202 'unsupported in v1' (Cursorial.UI.Xaml.Frontend/Parsing/XamlParser.cs:744, XamlDiagnosticCodes.cs:31-32). So a consumer can neither write `<ShapedColumn ...>` nor `new ShapedColumn<Order,decimal>(...)` against an object-typed grid. There is no bridge from a declarative, non-generic column description (path string, header, format, width) to the compiled kit, and no statement of which lambda-vs-path forms exist, what path grammar is supported (BindingPath.Parse handles indexers/attached segments; `Expression.Property` chains in §2.2 do not), or how sort options (culture, StringComparison, direction, group index, aggregates) surface per column.
upheld.amendment: Add to §3 a non-generic public DataGridColumn description type (plain data, no compiled state): FieldName (string path, documented as the property-chain subset of the BindingPath grammar — indexers/attached segments unsupported v1, diagnostic on use), Header (defaults from FieldName), Width : GridLength (existing XamlConverters converter), Format, Culture, StringComparison, SortDirection?, SortOrder, GroupIndex?, Aggregates (SummaryKind collection), and the §7-Q7 CellPainter seam. Specify resolution timing: the shaping controller resolves the runtime row type at attach (first ItemsSource) and compiles each column's kit from (resolvedRowType, FieldName, options) through the existing §2.2 codegen cache; ShapedColumn<T,TKey> becomes internal machinery DERIVED from DataGridColumn, not a public authoring type. For typed code-first use add DataGridColumn.For<T,TKey>(Expression<Func<T,TKey>> getter, ...) returning DataGridColumn with the expression stashed as accessor source, cache-keyed by column instance (lambdas cannot key by path). State the auto-generation rule (reflection over the resolved row type at attach) in the same section.

upheld.problem: SelectionModel's index space cannot serve a shaped view without new machinery, so 'as-is' is a false reuse claim with public-API consequences. (a) If selection lives in *view-index* space, every re-sort/filter/group toggle permutes the view wholesale — SelectionModel's only fixup hooks are contiguous insert/remove/move/reset (SelectionModel.cs:149-231); an arbitrary permutation is inexpressible, and its `Reindex` remapper is private (line 291). Selection would silently land on different rows after every reshape. (b) If selection lives in *row-id* (slot) space — the stable choice — `SelectRangeFromAnchor` breaks: it materializes the numeric interval [anchor..index] (lines 138-144), which is meaningless in slot space where contiguity is view-order. (c) Group rows occupy view indices; range selection and Ctrl+A must skip them — nothing in SelectionModel knows about non-selectable rows. (d) 'SelectedItem(s) in row-object terms' leaves pinned-down semantics undefined: what happens to a selected row that a filter change hides (retain-hidden vs drop-with-event)? What is `SelectedIndex` — view index (volatile, includes group rows) or something else? Consumers binding `SelectedItem` two-way will hit all of these on day one.
upheld.amendment: Replace §5's SelectionModel-as-is bullet and §3.3's selection line with a designed DataGridSelectionController component (in Cursorial.UI or DataViews per invariant 7; ListView/TreeListView consume it): selection STORED as stable row ids (slot ids per §2.1 — insert fixup is a no-op; row removal explicitly drops the id from the set before slot free-list reuse, firing SelectionChanged); gesture ranges COMPUTED over the current flattened view (walk anchor→target view positions, collect data-row ids, skip group-node entries — same skip for Ctrl+A); a snapshot-publish hook that remaps view positions after every reshape and applies a pinned HiddenRowSelectionPolicy (drop-with-event vs retain-hidden) for selected rows a filter change removed from the view. Public grid surface: SelectedItem : object? and SelectedItems : IReadOnlyList<object> (ids resolved through RowStore), CurrentCell : (int ViewRow, int Column); no view-index SelectedIndex (or, if kept for parity, document it as the volatile flattened-view position of the lead, -1 when hidden). Implementation choice: either wrap SelectionModel and add it a public bulk-set/Remap(Func<int,int>) API, or build the controller standalone over a HashSet<int> of ids; budget it as a real component with its own dataviews-matrix rows (reshape remap, hidden-row policy, group-skipping ranges, slot-reuse hygiene), not ~30 lines of gesture glue.

upheld.problem: The v1 model as specified is a flat AND of three lanes — there is no OR, no NOT, no grouping. The deferred Filter Builder in the UX spec (tokyo-night-terminal-datagrid.html, 'Filter Builder — visual condition tree' section) renders an And/Or condition TREE with group nodes. A tree cannot target a conjunction-of-lanes model: when the builder/text-language lands, the public filter API must be replaced, breaking every v1 consumer who set `Predicate`/value sets programmatically. The claim that the model is already expression-shaped is not true of what §2.4 actually describes.
upheld.amendment: Replace §2.4's public three-lane model with a criteria tree as the v1 public filter model: `FilterNode` = `And(children)` / `Or(children)` / `Not(child)` / `Comparison(column, op, value)` / `InSet(column, values)` / `Custom(Expression<Func<T,bool>> or delegate — code-only, not builder-visible)`. The checklist popup writes/replaces its column's `InSet` leaf, the auto-filter row writes `Comparison` leaves, the programmatic predicate is a `Custom` leaf; all compose under a root `And` by default, so v1 observable behavior is unchanged. Internal evaluation is unchanged: the controller folds the tree through the existing compiled filter kits into the §2.4 slot bitset. Convenience setters (`Predicate`, per-column value-set/condition APIs) remain as thin writers of the corresponding leaves. Amend §1's deferred note to state the builder/text parser target this same `FilterNode` tree additively (builder renders/edits it; parser produces it), and note `Custom` leaves render as an opaque "custom condition" node in the future builder.

upheld.problem: No controller type, factory, or non-generic facade is ever named, and the doc never explains how the non-generic grid binds an object-typed `ItemsSource` to the `<T>` engine. A consumer wanting shaping without the grid (sort/filter/group a collection, export the shaped view) has no documented entry point; the grid itself must do a `MakeGenericType`-style hop from the runtime element type to `DataViewController<T>` — unstated, and it interacts with the §0.8 AOT posture (fine under RequiresDynamicCode, but it must be *the* documented factory, not an accident inside the grid). Also unstated: the type-resolution policy for non-generic/heterogeneous `IEnumerable` (IEnumerable<T> interface? first item's type?), whether a controller can serve two views (collapse state lives on the controller per §2.5, which couples views), and what `IShapingScheduler` a dispatcher-less consumer gets (a unit test or server-side export must not need UIApplication).
upheld.amendment: Add a facade subsection to §2 (and reconcile §0.8/§2.6/§5 to it): (1) Name the typed headless-first entry point `DataViewController<T>` — Columns, SortDescriptions, GroupDescriptions, Filter (the condition tree), Summaries, Snapshot, SnapshotChanged, BeginBatch()/EndBatch(), collapse-state API — and a non-generic `IDataViewController` the DataGrid consumes (snapshot, descriptions, formatted-cell/format access; no TKey or T in its surface). (2) Make `DataViewController.Create(IEnumerable source, DataViewOptions options)` the single documented [RequiresDynamicCode] generic-instantiation site (the grid calls it, never its own MakeGenericType), with a pinned element-type resolution ladder: options.RowType override → the source's implemented IEnumerable<T> (most-derived unambiguous) → first-item runtime type → error on empty untyped source; note that §0.8's AOT-fallback seam covers BOTH ShapingCodegen and this factory, and that typed `new DataViewController<T>(...)` is the AOT-clean path. (3) Pin controller:view = 1:1 for v1 (ListView/TreeListView instantiate their own controller; "reuse" in §5 means the type, not the instance), making collapse/selection-state ownership unambiguous. (4) Pin the default IShapingScheduler to synchronous-inline (deterministic headless/server use with background shaping effectively disabled unless a scheduler is supplied); the UI adapter installs the frame-loop-aligned scheduler.

upheld.problem: One adjective is the whole story for the surface most consumers touch first. Undefined: the trigger (a bool property? Columns-empty implies auto?), the generation source (public readable properties of the resolved row type, in what order — reflection order is unspecified in .NET), header derivation, per-type defaults (numeric right-align + format, DateTime format, bool rendering), the customization hook, and the interplay when explicit columns co-exist (WPF *appends* auto columns after explicit ones; DevExpress populates only when empty — they differ, so it must be pinned). Without a customization event, any app that wants 'auto minus two columns, and format Amount as currency' is forced to abandon auto mode entirely.
upheld.amendment: Add an auto-column subsection to §3.1 (or a new §3.1a) pinning: `AutoGenerateColumns : bool` (default true) that is ignored whenever `Columns` is non-empty (the DevExpress populate-only-when-empty rule — simpler than WPF's append and avoids duplicate-column surprises); generation source = public instance readable properties of the resolved row type, ordered base-class-first then MetadataToken within each type (declaration order — pinned, since reflection order is otherwise unspecified); header = property name (seam for future humanization); per-type defaults matching the mockup — numeric key types right-aligned with a numeric format default, DateTime with a culture short format, bool rendered as the theme's check glyphs; a cancelable `AutoGeneratingColumn` event with a replaceable column, raised BEFORE the controller compiles kits (§2.2) so substituted columns compile exactly once; and an explicit statement that anonymous-type rows are supported (expression-compiled accessors reach internal anonymous-type properties) as a headline shaping scenario.

upheld.problem: The loader mechanics actually work for the happy path — a get-only `Columns : IList`-implementing property fills via the read-only-collection path (XamlObjectGraphBuilder.cs:631-744), and plain CLR objects with settable properties + the converter ladder instantiate fine — but two decisions must be made NOW because they are baked into the base class: (1) `{Binding}`/`{TemplateBinding}` throw unless the target is a `UIObject` (XamlMarkupExtensionHandler.cs:186,228), and `{DynamicResource}`/`SetResourceReference` needs tree-scoped lookup that a not-in-tree column can never satisfy — if `DataGridColumn`/`FormatRule` ship as POCOs, adding `Header="{Binding ...}"` later is a breaking base-class change (WPF made DataGridColumn a DependencyObject for precisely this). (2) Threshold/highlight rules declared in XAML carry literal values (`Value="100"`) whose target type is the *column's key type*, unknown to the loader (the rule property is `object`) — the string must survive to controller-attach time and coerce through the column kit, which the rule API must be designed for (store `object` raw + coerce on attach), otherwise XAML rules only work for strings. Predicate/Expression rules are code-only under CUR1202 — must be documented, not discovered.
upheld.amendment: Add a control-level object-model subsection to §3: (1) DataGridColumn and FormatRule derive from UIObject with property-system-backed (StyledProperty) members, following the BarCommand precedent — this makes Header="{Binding ...}" and future VM-driven column properties work through the loader's existing UIObject+UIProperty gate without a later breaking base-class change; (2) DataGrid.Columns is a get-only IList marked as the grid's [ContentProperty] so <DataGrid><DataGridColumn .../></DataGrid> fills via the loader's read-only-collection path; (3) spec the FormatRule value pipeline: rule Value/threshold members are typed object, hold the raw parse-time value (string from XAML), and coerce against the resolved column key type at controller attach using the same per-key-type literal parsers as the auto-filter condition compilers, with a CUR-band-style diagnostic on coercion failure; (4) document v1 XAML limits explicitly: no {DynamicResource} on columns/rules (SetResourceReference is UIElement-gated — UIObject derivation does not enable it), and Predicate/Expression rules are code-only (lambdas are not XAML-expressible).

upheld.problem: If the snapshot's public read surface is the raw packed `int[]`, the API freezes an encoding that cannot carry what the tree flatten needs: in a TreeListView every row is a DATA row that also carries structural facts (level, has-children, expanded) — the packed int distinguishes only data-row-vs-group-node, and per-data-row level/expander has nowhere to live. The §5 claim that 'rows + structural rows is exactly the tree flatten' is only true if the row-description surface is extensible; a raw-array API makes the tree adapter a breaking change, violating invariant 7.
upheld.amendment: In §2.5/§2.6: keep the packed int[] encoding internal to DataViewSnapshot. The public read surface becomes accessor methods returning structs: `int Count`, `ViewRowInfo GetRow(int viewIndex)` returning `{ bool IsGroup; int RowId; int GroupNodeIndex; byte Level }` (aggressively-inlineable decode of the internal packed entry, allocation-free), and `GroupInfo GetGroup(int nodeIndex)`. In §5, reword the tree-flatten claim: the tree adapter reuses the sort/filter/format kits and the view-permutation machinery, with `ViewRowInfo` widened ADDITIVELY (HasChildren/IsExpanded, and Level meaning tree depth) — not "exactly" the group flatten, since tree rows are data rows that simultaneously carry structure. The §3.2 painter and any future ListView consume only the struct surface, never the encoding.

refuted.claim: "The multi-column comparer is one compiled Comparison<int> reading the active key vectors ... All compilation happens once per shape change, cached per (rowType, path, culture, options)."
refuted.reason: The finding attacks an implementation the design did not choose. The engine code in the worktree (ShapedColumn.cs:45-47, 82-94) already binds compiled comparers to key vectors via Expression.Field(Expression.Constant(this), nameof(Keys)) — the array reference is reloaded per compare, with an explicit comment forbidding capturing the array into the tree — so geometric growth/Array.Resize is always observed: no orphaned arrays, no stale reads, no recompile-per-grow. The cache-key claim misreads the doc's two-tier compile story: the (rowType, path, culture, options) cache covers the instance-independent per-column kits (getter/Comparison<TKey>/formatter — no array state), while the fused Comparison<int> is compiled once per shape change (BuildSlotComparison), instance-bound by design and never shared-cached. The recommended SortContext's 'pinning for free' is redundant under §2.6's chosen semantics (mutations queue as pending ticks during a background run and replay after publish, so nothing writes key vectors mid-flight), and per-compare cost is identical (one indirection either way). All that remains is a one-sentence §2.2 doc clarification restating the field-load binding — a wording fix, not a design change.

refuted.claim: "Func<TKey,string> Formatter ... no box" and "MeasureOverride ... pre-composes the band's row content (formatted cell strings ...) into a pooled band cache — render never allocates."
refuted.reason: The finding's arithmetic is right (verified: ScrollContentPresenter.cs BandPadding = max(viewportRows, 8), BandLength = viewport + 2*padding, re-anchor past ±padding — so ~120-row bands shifting ~40 rows with 2/3 overlap, ~1,100 Func<TKey,string> calls per re-anchor), but its three load-bearing claims fail verification. (1) The technical premise is false on this repo's toolchain: I built and executed `Expression.Lambda<SpanFmt>(...).Compile()` for a custom `delegate bool SpanFmt(int v, Span<char> dst, out int written)` wrapping `int.TryFormat` on net10.0 — it compiled and ran correctly ("1,234,567"), so expression trees are NOT barred from producing span formatters; the doc's codegen route is not a dead end. (2) The promised payoff — "zero allocation per band fill" — is unachievable by the recommendation as scoped: the paint path itself is the dominant fling allocator. DrawingContext.DrawText allocates `cluster.ToString()` PER DRAWN GRAPHEME CLUSTER (DrawingContext.cs:751 and :761 — the `substitute` cache covers only tabs), so re-rastering a 120-row band allocates one ~24 B single-char string per visible character (thousands of strings, 2–4× the formatter strings), and the whole-band re-raster on re-anchor is the SCP granularity contract regardless of any formatter/ring cache. Pooled char buffers dead-end at the paint call; fixing this requires a Drawing-layer change the finding never identifies. This is the same "inherent per-frame repaint allocation — recorded perf debt" the existing VirtualizationFlingBenchmark documents, and that benchmark deliberately gates re-anchor frames by median TIME (33 ms), not bytes — 0 B contracts are scoped to steady-state/in-band slides, which the doc's §3.2/invariant-6 claims correctly mirror (band fill is measure-side; "render never allocates" is not falsified, and "no box" is literally true — string allocation isn't boxing). (3) Consequence is below the change threshold: ~50 KB of formatter strings and ~0.1 ms of ToString CPU per re-anchor frame against the 33 ms budget, only while actively flinging, in a lane already ~100× cheaper than the element-realizing alternative it deviates from. The recommendation's contract is also broken as specified: `where TKey : ISpanFormattable` excludes `string` AND `bool` (verified — neither implements ISpanFormattable; enums do), and the string formatter is needed regardless for cold surfaces the doc commits to (distinct-value checklist §2.4, GroupNode.FormattedKey §2.5), so span formatting is additively evolvable later (a TryFormatInto beside Formatter, defaulting through the string path) rather than a v1 one-way door. The genuinely valuable observation buried here — that fling-time allocation is dominated by per-cluster string churn — points at DrawText's `cluster.ToString()` (a single-char/ASCII string cache there would benefit every control, ListBox included), which is a different, smaller, engine-level fix, not the §2.2/§7-Q7 contract rewrite this finding demands.

refuted.claim: Inline editing is deferred behind an 'IDataGridEditorHost seam on columns' — i.e., cuttable later without rework.
refuted.reason: The finding's premise is false against the doc under review: inline editing is NOT deferred behind a column-side seam. There is no "IDataGridEditorHost" anywhere in dataviews-design.md. §1 explicitly puts "basic in-row editing" in v1 scope — "the edit-row element-hosting seam in the rows presenter + the TextBox editor path … the proof that the special case works end-to-end" — and the Deferred section defers only the full editor suite, which "rides the v1 edit-row host." §3.2 already specifies exactly the mechanism the recommendation asks to reserve: a DataGridEditRowHost presenter child arranged at the edit row's cell x-ranges, parent-before-children render order, hit-testable (verified against RenderTree.HitTest, whose leaf gate applies IsHitTestVisible "to this element only (children stay hittable)", RenderTree.cs:263/693), scrolling with content-frame bounds, with the band cache skipping the hosted row — i.e., v1 ships a working overlay host with a live TextBox editor, stronger than the finding's "reserved slot." The Q4 leg is also wrong on the facts: PART_AutoFilterRow is a separate template part OUTSIDE the ScrollViewer (§3.1 anatomy), an ordinary element host (§3.4 "hosts one lightweight text editor per column") that never scrolls vertically, never re-anchors, and is not inside the hit-leaf painter — so per-column filter TextBoxes are not "a second element-hosting scheme" competing with the presenter's mechanism, and Q4 remains a legitimate open cost question, not a seam-proof question. The only residual truth is minor: the mockup's .c-ind indicator column (✎/＊) is unmentioned in the doc — worth a sentence noting the column model admits a leading non-data column, but that is a doc gap editing's v1 implementation hits immediately, not a design change. Accepting the finding as written would change nothing in the design as it stands.

minors.claim: "per-row INPC ... one shared PropertyChangedEventHandler; the sender resolves to a row id" via a Dictionary<T,int>.
minors.problem: Unquantified at 1M rows: subscription is 1M event-adds at load and 1M event-removes on Reset (tens of ms, on the UI thread, inside the INCC handler); the reference-equality Dictionary<T,int> is ~50 MB at 1M entries; and the rows' PropertyChanged fields strongly reference the shared handler → the controller → the grid, so rows that outlive the grid keep the whole tree alive unless the teardown sweep runs (repo has prior art on exactly this leak class in static-event form).
minors.recommendation: Chunk (or background) the subscribe/unsubscribe sweeps on bulk load/Reset; make unsubscription part of the controller's TearDown contract and test it (leak-tracker style); record the ~50 MB dictionary + ~8 MB T[] + per-column key vectors in a memory-budget table so 1M-row sizing is a stated, not discovered, fact.

minors.claim: §2.7: "evaluation happens at paint for visible rows only, no caching (40×8 cells/frame)" vs §3.2: MeasureOverride "pre-composes ... conditional-format verdicts into a pooled band cache" and render draws from the cache.
minors.problem: The two sections contradict each other on where rules evaluate (paint vs band pre-compose) and on the volume (40 visible rows vs ~120 band rows); "per frame" is also wrong — steady-state frames re-raster nothing, so evaluation only happens at band fill / data tick. Additionally the DataBar's "column min/max anchors from the key vector" has no maintenance story under live ticks: removing the current extremum requires an O(N) rescan; done per tick it's another hidden full pass.
minors.recommendation: Pick the band-fill site (consistent with §3.2), fix §2.7's text and arithmetic, and pin DataBar anchor maintenance to once-per-publish (lazy O(N) rescan amortized into the tick pipeline's existing pass, or monotone-widen with periodic exact recompute) — never per-tick rescan.

minors.claim: "an int[] of packed entries (data row id | group node index)".
minors.problem: Packing two id spaces plus a discriminator into one int is unspecified; a tag bit halves the row-id space and the natural encoding mistake (high-bit tag with unsigned ids) collides with the a−b tiebreak arithmetic elsewhere if ids are ever compared raw.
minors.recommendation: Encode group nodes as negative values (~nodeIndex, the Array.BinarySearch idiom): row ids keep the full non-negative range, the discriminant is a sign test, no masking.

minors.claim: HandlesScrolling => true on the grid keeps arrow keys out of the ScrollViewer.
minors.problem: The gate is real (ScrollViewer.OnKeyDown returns unhandled when TemplatedParent is Control { HandlesScrolling: true }) but it is not the operative mechanism here: routed key events travel from the FOCUSED element up its ancestor chain, and with the grid as the focused one-tab-stop and rows drawn (nothing focusable inside the SCP), the template-child ScrollViewer is never on the route — it cannot see the keys at all. The gate only becomes load-bearing if focus ever lands inside the ScrollViewer subtree (e.g. the deferred inline editors).
minors.recommendation: Keep the override (correct defense-in-depth for the inline-editing future) but fix the stated mechanism: arrow/page keys are handled in DataGrid.OnKeyDown because the grid is the focus leaf; HandlesScrolling is the guard for the day focus lives inside the viewport.

minors.claim: Header/filter/footer presenters mirror ScrollViewer.HorizontalOffset for aligned column shift (their 1–2-row re-raster on H-scroll is trivial).
minors.problem: Re-raster granularity is per ZONE, not per element. The header/filter/footer presenters sit outside the SCP, i.e. inside the surface/window zone; an AffectsRender offset flip on them marks that whole zone raster-dirty, so every H-scroll tick re-rasters the entire window content (everything except SCP subtrees) — not 1–2 rows. At a 300-column grid in a full-screen window that is the most expensive per-keystroke invalidation in the app.
minors.recommendation: Make each band presenter its own render boundary (ClipToBounds = true is safe here — their bounds are 1–2 rows, unlike the rows presenter) so the H-offset re-ink is band-local; alternatively give each band an [AffectsComposite] slide over its own band-wide scene (they are little SCP-shaped strips: full-content-width scene, viewport-width clip, offset = composite parameter — zero re-raster on H-scroll, matching the rows viewport exactly).

minors.claim: Data ticks re-fill the band cache (formatted cell strings via the compiled Func<TKey,string> formatters); render never allocates.
minors.problem: Render is clean, but the fill path — the actual hot path under live ticks — allocates a string per cell per fill: a whole-band refill at band ≈ 3×viewport (~120 rows × 9–40 columns) is ~1–5k string allocations per tick and per re-anchor, sustained every frame under a ticking feed and during flings. That is steady Gen0 churn on exactly the path invariant 2's 'no boxing on hot paths' ethos targets, and 'ticks re-fill the band cache' as written re-formats clean rows too.
minors.recommendation: Two amendments: (1) refill only dirty rows on a tick (the DirtySet already knows them; whole-band refill only on re-anchor/reshape); (2) compile span formatters instead of Func<TKey,string> — the key types are ISpanFormattable, so codegen can emit TryFormat into a pooled char buffer per band row (delegate shape like SpanFormat<TKey>(TKey value, Span<char> destination, out int written)), making the tick path allocation-free end to end. Keep Func<TKey,string> only for cold consumers (group captions, filter checklist).

minors.claim: Keyboard: focusable header cells (§1) on a direct-draw header presenter (§3.1), with the grid 'Focusable one-tab-stop'; state looks come from styled brush properties on the presenter that the theme sets via SetResource setters.
minors.problem: Two under-specified mechanisms. (1) 'Focusable header cells' contradicts both the direct-draw header and the one-tab-stop model — drawn cells cannot hold framework focus, and there is no public focus-visible readback (only IsFocused/IsKeyboardFocusWithin mirrors; FocusVisible is InteractionState/pseudo-class only). Header-cell focus must be virtual (a grid-owned header focus index, cue drawn by the header presenter), with the :focus-visible gate reachable declaratively via a nested conditional rule on the grid ('^:focus-visible /template/ …' flipping a styled bool on the presenter — StyleTrigger lane, AffectsRender). (2) The presenters are not Controls, so they get no control theme through the contribution tier by default; the verified mechanisms are (a) the DataGrid theme's template building the presenters and calling SetResourceReference on them (the Bars precedent, Template lane, live on palette flips) or (b) implementing the public IControlThemeHost on the presenter (StyleEngine.cs:830 checks the interface, not Control) to receive a Type-keyed theme Style of its own.
minors.recommendation: Pin both in the doc: virtual header focus (grid-owned index + drawn cue + the nested :focus-visible rule), and pick one presenter-theming lane — implementing IControlThemeHost on DataGridRowsPresenter/header/footer presenters is the cleaner reusable choice (a consumer can re-theme the presenter without replacing the whole grid template) and needs no engine change.

minors.claim: 'The auto-filter row hosts one lightweight text editor per column; text parses through the column's condition grammar (>, >=, <, <=, =, bare text = contains/starts-with)'.
minors.problem: The mockup's filter row is not uniformly text: Region/Rep/Status cells are `(All) ▾` picker cells (distinct-value dropdown — the DevExpress auto-filter combo for low-cardinality columns), Order shows a ⌕ contains affordance, Date shows `≥ date`. The doc's uniform-TextBox model drops the per-column editor-kind dimension; the grammar also lacks not-equal (`<>`/`!=`), present in every DevExpress auto-filter grammar.
minors.recommendation: Make the filter-row cell kind a per-column option (Text | DistinctPicker | Disabled) — the DistinctPicker reuses the checklist popup anchored to the filter cell — and add `<>` to the operator grammar. Both are cheap now; the per-column editor-kind slot is also the natural forerunner of IDataGridEditorHost.

minors.claim: The interaction model (selection, keyboard, mouse) is complete for v1.
minors.problem: No copy-to-clipboard anywhere (v1 or deferred). This bites harder in a terminal than on the desktop: with SGR mouse tracking enabled the terminal's NATIVE text selection is unavailable over the grid, so users have no way at all to get data out — a regression versus a dumb `ps`-style listing. DevExpress ships CopyToClipboard/Ctrl+C as baseline. The infrastructure already exists: `Cursorial.Core/Output/ClipboardWriter.cs` (OSC 52) — the gap is purely a missing gesture + TSV/text serialization of the selected rows through the already-compiled formatters.
minors.recommendation: Add Ctrl+C = copy selected rows (visible columns, tab-separated, formatted values; header row optional flag) via ClipboardWriter/QueueControlSequence to v1 — it is a day's work on existing pieces — or at minimum list it in Deferred with the gesture reserved. Note OSC 52 write support varies by terminal; degrade silently.

minors.claim: PART_Footer renders the summary band; 'stacked multi-aggregate cells' are in scope; 'every view row is exactly one cell row … the footer band is outside the viewport'.
minors.problem: Consistent so far, but the mockup pins a behavior the doc never states: when any column carries ≥2 aggregates 'the footer band GROWS to two cell-rows tall' (`.grow.tall`), with per-cell stacked label/value rows — i.e., footer height = max aggregate count over columns, and single-aggregate cells vertically… (the mockup stretches them). If the footer presenter is speced as a 1-row band, stacking becomes a re-layout surprise; the group-summary editor also shows per-aggregate display-text templates ('Sum = {0}') and format strings distinct from the column's cell format, which the aggregator/formatter kit should carry as a per-summary format, not reuse the cell formatter.
minors.recommendation: State footer height = max(1, max per-column aggregate count) with muted-label/accent-value stacked rows per the mockup, and give each summary description its own format string + display template ('{0}' substitution) in the engine's aggregate descriptors — a field on the v1 API, trivial now, breaking later.

minors.claim: Horizontal scrolling with shared column offset; `GetExtent() = (totalColumnWidth, viewRowCount)` — width model otherwise unspecified.
minors.problem: No width type, no Auto policy, no star sizing is defined. Consumers will expect DevExpress 'best fit'; a naive Auto over 1M rows is an O(N) format sweep that violates the performance posture, and leaving it undefined guarantees an ad-hoc, hard-to-change behavior ships.
minors.recommendation: Reuse `GridLength` (`Auto`/`*`/absolute — converter already in XamlConverters.cs:404) + `MinWidth`/`MaxWidth` on the column. Pin Auto = header width ∨ widest formatted cell in the CURRENT BAND only (re-evaluated on re-anchor, monotonic-grow to avoid jitter), and expose an explicit `AutoFitColumn(column, int sampleRows)` API for deliberate full-fit. Star widths distribute viewport remainder after fixed/auto, DockPanel-style.

minors.claim: A `Dictionary<T,int>` (reference equality) maps row → id for INPC dispatch (reference-type rows; duplicate instances documented unsupported for INPC tracking).
minors.problem: The reference-equality identity map silently constrains the whole public API to reference-type rows, but nothing states it — a no-boxing engine invites struct/record-struct rows, which would either fail to compile the dictionary comparer or fall into ValueType.Equals boxing. And the duplicate-instance caveat scoped to 'INPC tracking' actually also breaks `SelectedItem` mapping and `ScrollIntoView(item)` — any object→id resolution.
minors.recommendation: Constrain honestly: `DataViewController<T> where T : class` in v1 (document it in the design, with a recorded seam — an `IRowIdentity<T>` comparer — for struct rows later), and widen the duplicate-instances caveat to cover every object→row-id API (selection by item, BringIntoView by item), not just INPC.

minors.claim: Header/keyboard gestures sort, group, and filter; 'keyboard + API grouping'.
minors.problem: The doc never names the observable shaping-state surface on the grid: consumers need to read AND write sort/group state programmatically and persist/restore layout (the DevExpress-grade expectation) — 'API grouping' with no named API. If gestures mutate internal controller state directly, two-way programmatic control gets bolted on later against the grain.
minors.recommendation: Expose `SortDescriptions` / `GroupDescriptions` as observable collections on the grid (mirrored into the controller; gestures edit the collections, glyphs render from them — one source of truth), plus a `GetLayout()/ApplyLayout()` serialization pair covering sort/group/filter/column widths/collapse state as a recorded v1.x seam.

openQuestionAnswers.answers:
Q1 (TimSort-only vs probe): TimSort-only, validated by the planned table — the probe hybrid is not worth its complexity. Evidence: (a) you must build the run-detection + galloping-merge core anyway for the repair path, so TimSort adds no marginal code; (b) .NET's Array.Sort(int[], Comparison<int>) wraps the delegate in a ComparisonComparer (interface dispatch + delegate call per compare), while a hand TimSort invokes the delegate directly — the introsort advantage on pure random is typically 10–25%, and with indirection-dominated compares (keys[view[i]] random loads) both are cache-miss-bound, shrinking the gap further; (c) the 'mostly-sorted' inputs that matter here (direction toggle = reversed runs → O(N) in TimSort; re-sort after incremental repairs = already sorted; correlated-column re-sort = long runs) are exactly TimSort's O(N) cases where introsort stays O(N log N). Keep the benchmark as the recorded justification, but design for TimSort-only.

Q2 (repair threshold): The premise needs correcting first — repair is Θ(N) memory traffic regardless of K (see findings), so the repair-vs-full-sort crossover is shallow: both are ~O(N)-traffic once the view is mostly sorted, and full TimSort on the post-burst view finds ~K+1 runs → O(N log K) compares vs the repair's O(N + K log(N/K)). A fixed N/8 default validated by the benchmark table is fine (the constant barely matters). The threshold that actually matters and is missing is the second axis: the V above which even the *tick pipeline* must leave the UI thread (finding 1) — that one should be measured (target: tick pipeline ≤ ~2 ms sync budget).

Q3 (O(V) group re-derive at 1M): Not acceptable. At 1M grouped rows the per-tick cost is two full O(V) passes (SameGroup walk + flatten rebuild) with ~8–16 MB of array writes plus compiled-delegate calls — 5–15 ms on the UI thread per coalesced tick, i.e. permanent dropped frames on the live-feed canary. But v1 does NOT need incremental group repair: route the whole tick pipeline (repair + re-derive + flatten) through the background lane above a size threshold, reusing the §2.6 snapshot/publish/replay machinery you're building anyway — O(V) off-thread at 1M is ~10 ms of ThreadPool time per coalesced tick, entirely acceptable. Record incremental group patching (repair already knows each dirty row's old/new view position → affected group paths; counts/aggregates patch O(K·levels); the flatten is the hard part) as a seam, not a v1 deliverable.

Q5 (sealed snapshot holes): Yes, three concrete holes — (1) free-list slot reuse can alias a row id that an in-flight shape or the currently PUBLISHED snapshot still references (queued Remove → freed slot → queued Add reuses it): defer slot reclamation until no snapshot references it (generation counter or refcount on the free list). (2) Extraction siting: 'key vectors it extracted before departure' puts O(N) extraction on the UI thread — move new-column extraction into the background phase over the sealed row-ref snapshot and document the torn-read-of-user-rows caveat. (3) Replay ordering: INCC + INPC pending ticks must be one FIFO replayed in arrival order (an INPC on a row a queued Remove targets must resolve against the pre-remove map), and a superseded shape's pending queue transfers whole to its successor. With those three pinned, sealed-vectors + replay strictly beats copy-on-write: COW of 1M-row key vectors is 10s of MB per shape and still needs the replay queue for INCC anyway. Also pin the comparer-context rule (finding 5): the background run reads arrays through its per-run context, never through live fields.

Q6 (direct-draw vs element rows): Full painter is right, and the codebase quantifies why: the element lane's re-anchor cost is real — VirtualizingStackPanel re-realizes its window via ItemContainerGenerator (UnrealizeOutside/RealizeRange), then measures every realized container, with the refine→invalidate loop under the LayoutManager fixpoint (VirtualizingStackPanel.cs MeasureOverride); at a ~120-row band × 9 columns that's container churn + styling + layout per re-anchor at fling cadence (~every K rows), where the painter's cost is formatting ~K rows into a cache. The middle ground (row = element, cells drawn) buys :alternate/ISelectableContainer idioms you can't use anyway once selection is row-id-keyed (finding 2) and hover is presenter state. One caveat to record: the painter forfeits per-row template extensibility — the ICellPainter seam (Q7) is the substitute and therefore load-bearing.

Q7 (ICellPainter from day one): Yes — and the formatter finding forces the seam's SHAPE now: expression trees cannot express Span<char> (ByRefLike types are rejected by System.Linq.Expressions), so the cell-content contract should be a span-writing formatter (ISpanFormattable-constrained generic helper, no codegen needed) + an ICellPainter that draws from the band cache's pooled char slices plus the typed key. Retrofitting from Func<TKey,string> later would break every column type's contract; defining it day one costs one interface. It is also the TreeListView/ListView reuse surface §5 promises.

Engine-claim verification summary (all against worktree code): the banding contract, ambient −BandStartRow zone translate (RenderTree.OnDrawZone:476), in-band composite slide (SCP.RunReAnchorCheck), re-anchor → InvalidateRealization → measure-before-raster ordering, the lifted 32K cap on the host path (MeasureWithHost caps at LayoutMath.MaxExtent ≈ 1.07B, so 1M view rows publish an exact uncapped Extent; the legacy 32K cap does NOT bite), hit-test content coordinates (HitZone adds ChildScrollOffset on descent, RenderTree.cs:668–669; MouseEventArgs.GetPosition → TranslateFromScreen folds the same), ScrollViewer.EnsureVisible(Rect) in content coordinates, dispatcher-job Phase 2 running before layout Phase 5 (a Post-coalesced repair lands same frame), AffectsRender existence, SetResource style setters + /template/ part rules (Bars precedent), and the DataViews InternalsVisibleTo (already in Cursorial.UI.csproj) all HOLD. Claims that do not hold as stated are in the findings (band window is internal-only, HandlesScrolling mechanism, header-band re-raster granularity, SelectionModel as-is, presenter theming lane).

Q3 (group re-derive O(V) per tick): NOT acceptable at 1M grouped rows — see the major finding. A K≪N tick pays an O(V) SameGroup walk + full flattened-view rebuild (~two 1M-entry passes + compiled-equality calls ≈ several ms) on the UI thread every coalesced tick, violating invariant 5 in the headline scenario. Either make the sync/background routing cost-based per cycle (an O(V) regroup above a V threshold rides the existing background lane) or patch groups/flatten by moved view ranges (the repair knows exactly which ranges moved).

Q4 (auto-filter editors): one real TextBox per visible column. The engine's text editing is element-bound — TextBox carries the caret via ITerminalCaretService (publication registry + transform leg + clip gating), selection, clipboard, and focus semantics; a 'drawn filter line' with a roving editor would reimplement caret publication, per-column edit-state commit/restore, and focus bookkeeping for zero measurable win (≤ ~40 visible columns of 1-row TextBoxes is trivial layout). Realize editors for visible columns only if column counts grow; revisit a roving editor only if in-presenter column virtualization (the recorded seam) ever lands.

Q5 (background snapshot): yes, holes — see the blocking finding. Sealed-vectors + pending-tick replay is sound ONLY with four pins: key vectors never written while a shape is in flight (INCC Add extraction deferred to replay), the free-list frozen mid-flight (no slot re-binding under an in-flight permutation), the shaper reading only departure-time array references and never _rows, and the synchronous small-repair lane suspended (queued) while a shape is in flight. Without these, slot reuse + in-place key writes produce an order-inconsistent comparer — TimSort merge-invariant corruption, not just wrong order. With them, sealed vectors beat copy-on-write (no per-shape copy of N×keys).

Q6 (direct-draw vs element rows): the full painter is right, on engine facts. (a) Raster cost is identical either way — the SCP zone re-rasters the whole band on re-anchor regardless of whether children paint it — so element rows ADD ItemContainerGenerator realize/unrealize, template expansion, style matching, and measure for ~band-length rows (≈ 3×viewport ≈ 120 rows × 9+ cells) per re-anchor on top of the same raster, and every fling re-anchor allocates (containers), forfeiting the steady-state 0 B posture. (b) The container idioms the middle ground would buy (:alternate, ISelectableContainer) are style-lane pseudo-class flips whose invalidation still lands as whole-zone re-raster — no granularity win. (c) Conditional formatting is per-cell and data-driven — it needs the painter anyway; styles can't express data-bar fills. One warning either way: the rows presenter must not become a render boundary (see the promotion-hazard finding), which the element-realizing lane also shares via VSP. Keep the element lane for TreeListView/ListView where per-row interactivity (editors, drag handles) earns its cost.

Q7 (ICellPainter from day one): yes. The presenter's Render otherwise hard-codes a column-kind switch (text/data-bar/badge), the deferred IDataGridEditorHost is already a per-column seam so a per-column paint seam is symmetric, and §5's ListView reuse means custom cells arrive before v2. Keep the seam shape band-cache-friendly: the painter receives the pre-composed cache entry + RenderContext + cell rect (paint-only, no data access, no allocation), so the zero-alloc render contract is enforced by the seam signature rather than by convention.

Q1/Q2 (TimSort vs probe hybrid; repair threshold): no engine-side evidence to pre-decide either; the doc's own benchmark-table-then-decide posture is right, and the ND25 harness conventions it cites exist. One engine note for Q2: the repair threshold should also consider the regroup cost (Q3) — K/N alone under-models the grouped case.

Q4 (auto-filter row editors — per-column TextBoxes vs roving editor): Roving single editor over a drawn filter line, decisively. Evidence: (1) the mockup renders filter cells as drawn wells/placeholders — visually identical to a painter, and only ONE cell can hold the caret at a time anyway, so N live TextBoxes buy nothing visible; (2) per-column live TextBoxes each need focus-stop registration, horizontal-offset mirroring, and theme templating — N elements re-laid out on every H-scroll, against the design's own direct-draw philosophy; (3) the mockup's filter row is heterogeneous (text cells, `(All) ▾` distinct-pickers, date), so the cell must be column-kind-driven regardless — a roving host materializing the column-provided editor on focus handles that uniformly; (4) most importantly, the roving overlay host is structurally the SAME mechanism deferred inline editing needs inside the viewport (see the editing-seam finding) — building it once for the filter row turns the editing deferral from 'hope' into a shipped, tested seam.

Q6 (direct-draw vs element-realizing rows — UX angle): The full painter is right for the v1 feature set: the mockup needs no per-cell interactive elements in the viewport (editors are deferred; the filter row is outside the viewport), and at 9 columns × ~120 band rows the element lane's per-re-anchor layout/styling cost buys nothing the painter can't draw. Two conditions: (a) reserve the overlay-child slot in the presenter (editing/filter roving host) so the painter isn't a dead end; (b) accept and DOCUMENT the customization consequence — there is no RowStyle/CellTemplate analog in the painter lane; all custom cell visuals must come through the painter seam (Q7), and app-level restyling comes only through the styled brush/attribute properties. The middle ground (row = element, cells drawn) is the worst of both: you pay container realization per re-anchor and still can't template cells.
