Q7 (ICellPainter as a day-one column seam): Yes. The mockup already demands at least six distinct cell renderings (plain text, data bar + value, badge + colored value, status glyph + tint, heat background, stacked summary cell), and the conditional-formatting taxonomy should grow to the mockup's six rule types (ColorScale/TopBottom finding) — without a painter seam every addition edits the presenter's draw switch. Make ICellPainter the unit the band cache pre-composes for (painter receives the formatted string + typed cell format struct + cell rect), ship the built-in painters through it, and custom columns (and future TreeListView indent/expander cells) come free. It also keeps the band-cache contract honest: pre-compose at measure, draw from cache at render, per painter.

Also settled from the mockup, not open in §7 but implied: the `ind-cur` current-row indicator glyph exists only in the mockup's CSS (never used in markup outside editing rows), so deferring the indicator column with editing is faithful to the spec — provided the column-geometry model admits a leading non-data column later.

Q4 (auto-filter editors — per-column TextBoxes vs one roving TextBox): Roving single editor. Evidence: (a) §3.2's whole economy is 'the presenter is the single hit leaf' — a rack of live TextBoxes would be the only element-realizing band in the control, re-introducing per-column layout/styling cost and a second focus-management regime (each TextBox is a tab stop; the grid is 'Focusable one-tab-stop' per §3.1, so N editors contradict the anatomy); (b) the deferred inline-editing seam (`IDataGridEditorHost`, §1) is exactly 'materialize one editor over the focused cell' — the roving filter editor is the same mechanism rehearsed early, so building it v1 de-risks the deferred feature instead of building a throwaway alternative; (c) horizontal alignment is free — the drawn filter line mirrors HorizontalOffset like the header already does, whereas a TextBox rack needs a mirroring panel. Cost: the drawn line must render text + a caret for the non-focused columns' stored conditions, but that's plain cell painting.

Q6 (direct-draw vs element rows): The full painter is right for the DataGrid — the ~3×viewport-row band at 9+ columns makes per-re-anchor container realization + styling genuinely worse, and `DrawnContentPresenter` (Cursorial.UI/Controls/DrawnContentPresenter.cs) shows the idiom is already sanctioned. But accept it WITH its API consequence stated: there is no DataTemplate/pseudo-class escape hatch for rows, so (1) every state look must be a styled presenter property (the doc says this) and (2) cell-visual extensibility has exactly one possible door — the Q7 painter seam. The middle ground (row=element, cells drawn) buys `:alternate`/ISelectableContainer idioms the presenter properties already replace, at re-anchor cost — not worth it for the grid; note it stays available to ListView per §5's 'pick per density'.

Q7 (ICellPainter from day one): Yes, and it changes the band-cache contract, which is why it can't be retrofitted cheaply. §3.2 pre-composes 'formatted cell strings' — a string-shaped cache bakes in text-only cells; DataBar/badge painting already special-cases around it, and any custom column (sparkline, icon+text, progress) would require forking the presenter since direct-draw offers no template escape (Q6). Make the cache entry a per-cell prepared struct produced by the column's painter (`ICellPainter.Prepare(rowId, key vectors…) → CellRun` at band-fill; `Paint(in CellRun, RenderContext, rect, state)` at render), with the built-in text/bar/badge painters as the three stock implementations. This also serves the §1 deferred editor host (painter and editor pair naturally on the column) and the §5 ListView reuse (ListView cells are the same painter interface over the flat view). Keep it internal-shaped but public: the 0 B steady-state gate applies to stock painters; document that a misbehaving custom painter owns its allocations.

Q3 (partial, API-visible angle only): whatever the incremental-group decision, do NOT let it leak into the snapshot read surface — the accessor-struct shape recommended in the findings (GetRow/GetGroup) keeps 'groups re-derived O(V)' vs 'groups repaired' invisible to consumers, so v1 can ship re-derive and change later without API impact.
